sources.title: Introducing Perceptron Mk1.5
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). September 25 launch identifies Mk1.5 and new native audio, tracking and tool capabilities. Its original benchmark tables compare task scores and its Mk1 comparison measures latency; none publishes a nominal total or active count, or identifies a named count-bearing base model. The nominal 32K context differs from current API documentation.

sources.title: Perceptron Mk1.5 model specifications
sources.evidence: Fresh direct Markdown retrieval October 27, 2026, 17:32 UTC (HTTP 200). Exact model ID, 36,864 shared context, 8,192 maximum output, text/image/video/audio inputs, reasoning and function calling. No nominal total, active count, named base-model lineage or architecture specification.

sources.title: Mk1.5 release notes
sources.evidence: Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded. September 25 launch entry independently confirms availability and shared 36,864-token context, optional video soundtracks, reasoning effort and caller-managed function calls.

sources.title: Mk1.5 tokenization guide
sources.evidence: Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded. Input conversation plus generated-output budget must fit one shared context. Audio cap is separate. Discusses visual preprocessing and cached prompt accounting without disclosing the neural architecture.

sources.title: Mk1.5 reasoning controls
sources.evidence: Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded. reasoning_effort accepts none, minimal, low, medium and high; none disables reasoning, other tiers enable it. Reasoning is separate from the final answer and consumes the output budget.

sources.title: Mk1.5 tool calling
sources.evidence: Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded. The model chooses declared functions and emits tool_calls. The caller executes them and returns results. A function named search does not activate a hosted search service.

sources.title: Perceptron Terms of Use
sources.evidence: Service access has restricted licenses; model-weight access and on-premises deployment require enterprise rights. Perceptron retains model intellectual property. Supports a Proprietary classification, not an open license.

sources.title: Perceptron home page
sources.evidence: Offers API access and separately negotiated commercial licenses to weights; no public Mk1.5 checkpoint release is provided.

sources.title: Teaching VLMs to think visually
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27 (HTTP 200). June 18 original training study calls its experimental model Isaac — 9B base. Its supervised and RL variants are not identified as Mk1.5; the 9B nominal size therefore does not establish this model’s count.

sources.title: Composing Weight and Data Sparsity in MoE
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27 (HTTP 200). January 21 original research upcycles Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B into experimental sparse models and compares Isaac 0.2. Published size/active labels describe those experiments and comparators, not Mk1.5; no Mk1.5 lineage is stated.

sources.title: SkillRater: Untangling Capabilities in Multimodal Data
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27 (HTTP 200). February 13 original research explicitly uses an Isaac 0.2-based inner model, 1B/2B training scales, and separate approximately 50M raters with SigLIP 400M features. No named Mk1.5 relationship supports transferring these counts.

sources.title: Isaac 0.5: Percepts Scale Control
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened original 52-page PDF October 27; also inspected full extracted text from the parent’s HTTP 200 fetch at 15:57 UTC. Section 3.1 and Table 11 explicitly give Isaac 0.5 36B total and 2.5B active at the 50% null-routing reference. Section 2.2 separately names Perceptron Mk1 as an annotation model. Tables 4–11 contain nominal active-size cost proxies or active/total columns for named comparators, but no Mk1.5 row or count-bearing lineage; Mk1.5 is absent from the full text.

sources.title: Perceptron publication index
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27 (HTTP 200): Mk1.5 remains the newest model publication, dated September 25. Rechecked linked original research and Isaac 0.5 comparison tables. Bounded fresh searches for Mk1.5 total, active/activated parameters, named base/fine-tune relationships and later original papers found no qualifying nominal disclosure; this is the search outcome, not proof that no disclosure exists anywhere.

sources.title: PerceptronAI public checkpoint inventory
sources.evidence: Fresh official organization API retrieval October 27, 17:32 UTC (HTTP 200) lists Isaac 0.1, Isaac 0.1 Base, Isaac 0.2 2B Preview, Isaac 0.2 1B and Isaac 0.5; no Mk1.5 checkpoint or card supplies parameter evidence.

sources.title: Perceptron releases 35B Mk1.5 model for embodied agents
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. Secondary lead only: despite its 35B headline, the body says the official announcement leaves parameter count unstated and attributes 35B to rohanpaul_ai’s breakdown. Followed both the social claim and official launch to their original X records; this article is not an independent measurement or developer specification.

sources.title: Rohan Paul Mk1.5 commentary
sources.evidence: Direct X page returned 403; X-owned syndication returned HTTP 200 October 27, 17:33 UTC for this exact status, author rohanpaul_ai, September 25. The returned excerpt calls Mk1.5 35B and quotes Perceptron’s launch post, whose text gives no count. This is a third-party assertion without a disclosed measurement or supporting developer count, so it is not adopted. The long-form post body is not included in syndication.

sources.title: Perceptron AI Mk1.5 launch announcement
sources.evidence: Direct X page returned 403; exact original status recovered through X-owned syndication with HTTP 200 October 27, 17:33 UTC. The September 25 official announcement describes embodied tasks and one model without platform-specific retraining; it supplies no nominal size, active count or named base model.

sources.title: Armen Aghajanyan on the Mk1.5 release
sources.evidence: Direct X page returned 403; exact original status excerpt recovered through X-owned syndication with HTTP 200 October 27, 17:33 UTC. The September 25 excerpt explicitly describes new architectures (2–4x speedup), audio as a first-class modality, and new post-training. It quotes the official Mk1.5 launch. This is evidence against assuming unchanged architecture from an unnamed predecessor, but does not disclose counts or enough topology to classify architecture. The long-form post body is not included in syndication.

sources.title: Perceptron: About us and model family
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. Official page identifies Armen Aghajanyan and links his X account, establishing the launch commenter’s first-party role. Separately lists Mk1.5, Mk1 and Isaac releases; supplies no count or explicit count-bearing base-model lineage for Mk1.5.

sources.title: Perceptron documentation index
sources.evidence: Fresh HTTP 200 retrieval October 27, 17:33 UTC. Inspected model, release-note and API-reference entries for size/architecture disclosures; current exact Mk1.5 model document is the linked specification. No parameter-count or technical-report entry establishes a missed named-base or active-count disclosure.

name.note: Exact name and API ID; distinct from Mk1 and Isaac releases.

developer.note: First-party announcement and terms identify the developer.

family.note: Product-series grouping for the named Perceptron family, not an assertion of identical underlying weights.

release_date.note: Same-day public availability is explicit in announcement and API release notes.

open_weights.note: API and negotiated commercial weight access; no open Mk1.5 checkpoint in the official public inventory.

license.note: Descriptive classification of restricted service and enterprise weight terms, not an SPDX identifier.

parameters_b.note: Fresh original-source and later-comparison searches found no published nominal Mk1.5 total or explicit named base with a supported transferable size. The 35B claim traces to Rohan Paul, not a developer specification or original measurement. Isaac 0.5’s 36B is a distinct model; the Mk1.5 launch also describes new architectures and added audio, so family succession alone does not justify inheriting a count.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked active parameters separately, including original Isaac 0.5 comparison Tables 4–11 and bounded searches for later Mk1.5 active/activated-parameter tables. No exact Mk1.5 row or published activation convention was found. Isaac’s 2.5B null-routing reference cannot be transferred, and no active count is inferred from the unsupported 35B total claim.

architecture.note: No Mk1.5 topology disclosure in accessed evidence. Generic VLM language, caching, third-party tokenizer matches and Isaac attention/MoE experiments do not establish this model’s architecture.

context_window.note: Retain current precise first-party shared context limit. Launch blog says nominal 32K; the discrepancy remains recorded, without inventing an input/output allowance explanation. Maximum output is 8,192 within the shared budget.

modalities.note: Native audio input is documented; video soundtrack processing is opt-in. Points, boxes, polygons, temporal clips and tracks are text/structured annotations, not generated image/video/audio media.

reasoning.note: Optional explicit reasoning-effort modes and separate reasoning output are documented.

tool_call.note: Model-generated custom function requests are supported. Execution and tool credentials belong to the caller; demo web search/sub-agents do not imply built-in API execution.

description.value: Multimodal model for visual grounding, video tracking and audio understanding, with optional reasoning and function calling.
description.note: Concise description supported by exact-variant API documentation; no inferred architecture or autonomous execution claim.

patch.description: Multimodal model for visual grounding, video tracking and audio understanding, with optional reasoning and function calling.
patch.notes: Current first-party API documentation specifies a shared 36,864-token context and 8,192-token output maximum; the launch announcement states nominal 32K. Video soundtracks require opt-in. Spatial and temporal outputs are structured annotations; the application executes function calls. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed: the third-party 35B claim is unverified, and no named base model with a published size is documented. Isaac 0.5’s 36B/2.5B counts describe a separate model. Mk1.5 adds audio and architecture changes; its topology remains unspecified.

sources.label: Mk1.5 release: architecture changes and audio

summary: Parameter re-audit October 27: total and active remain undisclosed after fresh exact-model documentation, original launch posts, related research, original active-count comparison tables and later-paper searches. Traced the unsupported 35B claim to third-party commentary; Isaac 0.5’s 36B/2.5B and experimental Isaac sizes lack Mk1.5 lineage. A first-party launch excerpt describes new architectures and audio. Explicit null patch values and parameter provenance added; the other twelve field assessments are unchanged.
